items.name: MiniMax H3
items.summary: Generates up to 15 seconds of 2K video with stereo sound from text plus up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips as references, and edits existing clips.
items.why: Open weights let a lab keep the exact model version for replication; in the EU, UK, US and South Korea, use needs MiniMax's approval.
items.imgAlt: MiniMax H3 announcement banner: the model's name over a violet jellyfish
items.credit: Picture: banner from MiniMax's official H3 announcement

items.name: Seedance 2.5
items.summary: Generates up to 30 seconds of video with synchronized sound in one pass, carries a scene on over several rounds with the same characters, and edits single timestamps, camera moves or a green-screen background.
items.why: A scene can be held constant while one cue changes, which is what an experimental manipulation needs.
items.imgAlt: Still from ByteDance Seed's one-take demo: a singer in a green sequined dress steps out on stage
items.credit: Picture: still from an official ByteDance Seed demo clip

items.name: Genie 4
items.summary: Generates worlds from text or an image in real time, now with sound and dialogue. Typed instructions change the weather, the camera or who is in the scene as you explore.
items.why: A participant can act inside a scene that keeps responding, instead of watching a fixed clip.
items.imgAlt: Frame from Google DeepMind's Genie 4 video: a crowned crane walks across snow while a text prompt is typed into the world, with the W A S D keys shown
items.credit: Picture: frame from Google DeepMind's official Genie 4 video on YouTube

items.name: PixVerse R2
items.summary: A real-time world you move through with the keyboard, with its own sound. Text, images or audio change it mid-session, and it remembers what has happened so far.
items.why: Because it remembers within a session, a participant's earlier choices can still shape the world later on.
items.imgAlt: Thumbnail of PixVerse's official R2 video: three generated worlds side by side, a fantasy kingdom, a cyberpunk city and an alien planet, linked by prompts
items.credit: Picture: thumbnail of PixVerse's official R2 video on YouTube

items.name: Atlas
items.summary: World Labs' new world model: from text, images or video it makes camera-controlled video up to a minute long, 360° panoramas, and 3D scenes as Gaussian splats.
items.why: Scenes come out in 3D that can be explored in a headset, and World Labs says Atlas will power future versions of Marble.
items.imgAlt: Atlas announcement picture: a figure on a cliff holds up a glass globe of clouds

items.name: Marble
items.summary: Builds lasting 3D worlds from text, photos, video or a rough 3D layout, which can be edited, expanded and combined, then exported as Gaussian splats, meshes or video.
items.why: A lab can build one scene, freeze it, and show every participant exactly the same world in a headset.
items.imgAlt: Picture from World Labs' Marble announcement: the ruins of a Roman amphitheatre under a blue sky

items.name: HY-World 2.0
items.summary: Turns text or a single image into a 3D world, or rebuilds one from photos or video, and outputs meshes and Gaussian splats that can go into a game engine.
items.why: Released openly on GitHub and Hugging Face, so a lab can run it on its own machines and keep the exact version.
items.imgAlt: HY-World 2.0 teaser: generated worlds in glass bubbles around the model's name
items.credit: Picture: teaser from Tencent's HY-World 2.0 repository

items.name: Meshy 7
items.summary: Turns a single picture, or four views, into a textured 3D model whose shape closely follows the picture.
items.why: Props for a 3D scene: one object can be swapped between conditions, such as a weapon for a phone.
items.imgAlt: Meshy 7 launch picture: a cartoon mouse adventurer beside its untextured 3D model

items.name: Xreal Aura
items.summary: See-through AR glasses on Android XR, with a 70° view, hand tracking and Gemini, wired to a pocket-sized computer. Sold in the US, Canada, Japan and South Korea, from $1,099.
items.why: Generated people and objects can appear in the participant's own room rather than in a fully virtual one.
items.imgAlt: Xreal Aura glasses on a black background

items.name: Meta VR Glasses
items.summary: VR in a pair of glasses of about 100 grams: 5K micro-OLED displays, full-colour passthrough, control by eyes and hands, and a tethered compute puck. $1,299.99, on sale from spring 2027.
items.why: Light enough for long sessions, and full-colour passthrough keeps the real room in view when needed.
items.imgAlt: A man wearing Meta VR Glasses

items.name: Meta Ray-Ban Display
items.summary: AI glasses with a small display in view, now also sold in Germany, France and Italy. New features include step-by-step directions and video calls as a lifelike avatar (US first).
items.why: A prompt or a short scene can appear in a participant's view during a field study, without a headset.
items.imgAlt: A woman wearing Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses
